## Research Question

task. State which series are analysed and why the question is suitable for
annual time series methods.

## Data

Describe the source, time span, variables, units, and any cleaning decisions.
Use `outputs/tables/series_summary.csv` to check the final analysis window.

## Exploratory Analysis

Discuss the main visual features of the two series. Refer to trend, turning
points, persistence, changes in variability, and the first-difference plots.

## Candidate Models

Explain the benchmark, trend, ARIMA, and state-space candidates used in the R
workflow. Link each model choice to the patterns seen in the exploratory plots
and ACF diagnostics.

## Model Diagnostics

Summarise residual checks and Ljung-Box results. Identify where residual
autocorrelation remains and what that means for model adequacy.

## Forecast Evaluation

Use the holdout accuracy table to compare models. Report the selected model for
each series and justify the selection using both accuracy and diagnostics.

## Final Forecasts

Present the final forecasts and describe uncertainty bands. Interpret the
forecasts carefully, noting any limitations caused by structural changes or the
annual sample size.

## Conclusion

Answer the research question directly. Keep the conclusion tied to the evidence
from the selected models and diagnostics.
